prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1497; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the left lane of a multi-lane roadway in Katy, Texas, when Driver 2 attempted to change lanes into the same space and made contact with the left rear quarter panel of Driver 1's vehicle. The contact was a sideswipe and both vehicles remained upright after the collision. Driver 1 was seated behind the wheel at the time, and a Passenger was also present in the vehicle. Responding officers spoke with both drivers, the Passenger, and two independent witnesses, all of whom gave accounts consistent with the sequence of events described at the scene. Photographs taken at the location show scrape marks and dented body panels on the left rear of Driver 1's vehicle and a matching area of damage on the right front of Driver 2's vehicle. No prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle was noted or reported. Driver 1 stated having pain in the neck and lower back shortly after the impact and was evaluated at the scene. The reported symptoms are consistent with the forces typically involved in a collision of this type. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved.
